title: SWAP Core Architecture Invariant Audit for Automatic-Weir Readiness

invariants.name: one computational kernel
invariants.application: automatic control is a reusable policy component, not a separate SWAP version

invariants.name: kernel separated from IO
invariants.application: IMPEND/INTWL/date parsing remains in adapters/runtime

invariants.name: explicit data separation
invariants.application: period parameters, WLSTAR state, scalar hydraulic inputs, numerical history and results are distinct

invariants.name: compact persistent state
invariants.application: only WLSTAR is conditional control memory for SWMAN=2; no copied hydraulic arrays

invariants.name: scratch per worker
invariants.application: iphase and threshold-comparison intermediates are ephemeral scratch

invariants.name: scalable memory layout
invariants.application: phase tables are immutable/shareable and SWMAN=2 state is one scalar per active column

invariants.name: transactional timesteps
invariants.application: trial WLSTAR cannot mutate committed WLSTAR; D6 owns commit/rollback

invariants.name: cheap recomputation and warm start
invariants.application: control target is deterministic from committed WLSTAR, explicit event and hydraulic summary

invariants.name: generic time
invariants.application: legacy day arithmetic is translated into explicit events; drop rate uses generic dt

invariants.name: flexible coupling windows
invariants.application: control events subdivide arbitrary coupling windows rather than requiring midnight boundaries

invariants.name: coupling first-class
invariants.application: control memory and surface-water state remain rollback-capable for coupled predictor/corrector trials

invariants.name: explicit groundwater interface contract
invariants.application: groundwater_level enters through a hydraulic summary, not MODFLOW awareness

invariants.name: mass conservation absolute
invariants.application: D5 changes target/control state only; actual supply/discharge mass stays D3/D4/D6 first-class and no concession is introduced

invariants.name: interface sensitivities first-class
invariants.application: capacity-policy uncertainty is exposed rather than hidden; no fabricated tangent at held branches

invariants.name: limit coupling costs
invariants.application: phase selection is O(number of phases) with small bounded tables and no full reruns

invariants.name: MultiSWAP primary use case
invariants.application: three-scalar hydraulic summary and compact WLSTAR state are batch-friendly

invariants.name: no mandatory one-to-one MODFLOW relation
invariants.application: control policy knows no MODFLOW cell fractions or external topology

invariants.name: deep-vadose optional separate component
invariants.application: no deep-vadose responsibility

invariants.name: mass-conserving component transitions
invariants.application: control target changes do not silently create supply/discharge mass

invariants.name: alternative soil-water solvers remain open
invariants.application: control consumes solver-neutral hydraulic summaries

invariants.name: reuse SWAP physics maximally
invariants.application: frozen threshold and drop-rate semantics are reconstructed without retaining legacy globals

invariants.name: other modules not coupled to HeadCalc internals
invariants.application: selected pressure head is supplied as a scalar; no H array or NODHD traversal inside control

invariants.name: physics options and solver policy separated
invariants.application: automatic weir management is physical control; WLSBAK/OSSWLM and retry policy remain numerical

invariants.name: predictable compute time
invariants.application: phase evaluation is bounded; held capacity discrepancy fails closed rather than invoking unbounded correction

invariants.name: reference mode available
invariants.application: exact source-order threshold evaluation remains the reference route

invariants.name: diagnostics part of runtime
invariants.application: selected phase, event flag, target change, drop-rate limiting and capacity-policy hold are explicit diagnostics

invariants.name: optional functionality scales with use
invariants.application: WLSTAR state and automatic phase data are required only for SWMAN=2 columns

invariants.name: runtime/coupler organizes composition
invariants.application: runtime resolves events and composes D3/D4/D5/D6; policy does not own global topology

invariants.name: no silent dependencies
invariants.application: no implicit day, midnight, file or MODFLOW dependency is retained

invariants.name: every architecture change audited
invariants.application: all 30 invariants are explicitly checked here with eleven source holds

hard_holds: do not retain legacy calendar arithmetic inside kernel
do not treat WLSBAK or NUMADJ as physical control state
do not choose a SWQHR1/SWQHR2 capacity-head reconciliation without separate scientific qualification
do not evaluate fractional SWQHR1 power on negative WOVER
do not reintroduce D4 inconsistent overflow-fallback state
do not hide the DROPR=0.001 or DISCAP=WDIS branch seams
